full_cake_replacement.description: Replaces the NVIDIA stack end-to-end. Examples: AMD Helios, hyperscaler custom silicon (where applicable).

fabric_alternatives.description: Replaces ONLY the fabric layer within the cake. The rest of the NVIDIA stack remains.

uec_coalition.description: Ultra Ethernet Consortium members — open-standard fabric coalition. Includes AMD, Cornelis, Broadcom, hyperscalers. Broadcom designs hyperscaler chips, making them a double enabler.

provenance.source: Ultra Ethernet Consortium public member roster.

components.name: AMD Helios (MI455X / MI450)
components.positioning: Full-stack replacement. Helios rack = 72x MI455X (analogous to NVL72), targeting Q3 2026.
components.moat_framing: AMD has hardware parity / a memory-bandwidth edge, but ROCm has NOT reached CUDA's ecosystem maturity, and TensorRT-LLM is NVIDIA-only and won't run on ROCm.

provenance.source: AMD MI455X / Helios announcement materials (per user-supplied competitor brief).
provenance.notes: AMD's own announcement figures for a pre-launch product (Helios targeting Q3 2026). Vendor-claim, not a shipping datasheet measurement — pill renders CLAIMED so the evidentiary weight reads honestly alongside cited NVIDIA datasheet specs in head-to-head views.
Pre-launch announcement figure; pill renders CLAIMED to distinguish from independent / datasheet citations.
Pre-launch announcement figure; pill renders CLAIMED to distinguish from independent / datasheet citations.

components.name: Hyperscaler Custom Silicon (TPU v7 / Trainium 3 / Maia 200 / MTIA 400)
components.positioning_scope: Hyperscaler segment ONLY — internal workloads. ADDITIVE to NVIDIA, not replacement: hyperscalers use custom silicon for internal training/inference and NVIDIA for MERCHANT cloud (external customers want CUDA).

provenance.source: Per-query inference savings cited at ~30-60% for internal workloads on custom silicon vs NVIDIA.
provenance.notes: Vendor-claimed figure on internal workloads only. Does not transfer to merchant cloud.

provenance.source: Merchant cloud customers want CUDA — NVIDIA wins this slice. Hyperscaler custom silicon does not address external customers.
provenance.notes: Re-tagged from cited to directional in phase 3c-0 — this is an analytical assertion about merchant-cloud preferences, not a specific independent citation or vendor benchmark. Directional band better matches the evidentiary shape.

provenance.source: Analyst coverage of hyperscaler internal-workload adoption of custom silicon (additive to NVIDIA).
provenance.notes: Range estimate from public analyst coverage; verify against specific reports.

components.name: Broadcom Jericho / Tomahawk Ethernet
components.positioning: Within-cake fabric swap. Broadcom also designs hyperscaler custom chips — double enabler.

provenance.source: Broadcom positioning emphasizes merchant-silicon Ethernet flexibility vs NVIDIA's integrated stack.

components.name: Arista Ethernet (7800R-class)
components.positioning: Within-cake fabric swap. Standard high-density Ethernet leaf-spine.

provenance.source: Arista positioning emphasizes open Ethernet vs vendor-locked fabric.

components.name: Cornelis CN5000 (Omni-Path, current gen)
components.positioning: Within-cake fabric swap. CN5000 400G Omni-Path → CN6000 800G RoCEv2 (2026) → CN7000 1.6T UEC (2027).

provenance.source: Cornelis CN5000 Omni-Path Switch Product Brief.

fabric_latency.text: Cornelis claims 45% lower latency vs 400G InfiniBand NDR

provenance.notes: Vendor benchmark — NOT a neutral measurement. Compare-against is NVIDIA Quantum-2 NDR 400G.

scale_conditional.small_scale: Cornelis wins — small-node HPC. Vendor cites 2x application speedup on 8-node HPC.
scale_conditional.large_scale: NVIDIA wins via SHARP / NCCL — in-network compute advantages emerge at large scale.
scale_conditional.breakpoint: Cornelis advantage erodes as cluster scales beyond ~16-32 nodes; SHARP/NCCL gap widens with node count.

provenance.claimed_by: cornelis (small-scale claim); cited (large-scale via NVIDIA SHARP docs)
provenance.source: Cornelis 2x app speedup on 8-node HPC is vendor-claimed. NVIDIA SHARP/NCCL large-scale advantage is documented public knowledge.
Cornelis pricing positioning — typically below NVIDIA per-port at director-class scale, above merchant Ethernet.
Cornelis positioning emphasizes tail-latency determinism and MPI tightly-coupled HPC — buyers chose Cornelis when raw collective-op performance at small/medium scale is the priority.
